native_declaration.source_behavior: On growth, native reserves first then copy-constructs every new slot from the supplied reference. It publishes mySize only after all constructions succeed. On copy exception, prior Size and values remain; successfully constructed untracked tail objects are not destroyed by Clear because they lie beyond mySize.
native_observations: Reserved-capacity growth copy-constructs each added slot: two copies, zero moves.
Reallocation moves the existing item once, then copy-constructs both new items; final capacity is three for the tested request.

When the second fill copy throws, capacity remains four and Size remains one. After vector destruction only the original and fill object are destroyed; the completed untracked tail object's destructor is not called.

rust_mapping.behavior: resize_with_value_ref clones each new slot individually under LengthRollback; the existing owned-value resize_with_value delegates to it. Size and prior elements roll back after Clone panic, and successfully cloned tail elements are dropped.
known_gaps: Native raw-storage exception cleanup leaves completed untracked tail objects undestroyed; Rust drops them during rollback.
Safe borrowing cannot pass an existing element of the same LinearVector while mutably resizing it, including native in-capacity self-alias use.
The separate with_value(size, value) Rust constructor was not changed in this slice; native's fill constructor delegates to Resize(size, value) and merits its own clone-versus-final-move audit.
